findings.evidenceJa: 今の衛宮士郎にとって、一番古い記憶
findings.governingReading: This is the oldest memory belonging to the present person called Emiya Shirou, with the name rubied as “self.”
findings.explanation: The English removes the qualification and name/self construction connecting the fire memory to Shirou’s present identity.

findings.highlight: make use of what has gone away
findings.evidenceJa: 失ったモノを生かす事
findings.governingReading: Only by affirming the past can Shirou keep what was lost alive or give it continuing life.
findings.explanation: Make use recasts memorial continuation as utilitarian exploitation and weakens the philosophy joining affirmation to the lost.

findings.evidenceJa: どのくらい眠っていたのか
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese moves from waking in bodily heat directly to inferring that he fell asleep in the shed; the duration question is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores a deleted thought and changes the opening rhythm and uncertainty.

findings.highlight: There is Saber’s figure, looking like she wants to complain to me.
findings.evidenceJa: なんだか文句を言いたそうな、セイバーの姿があった
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese contains Saber’s direct rebuke but comments out the narrator’s extra description of her looking ready to complain.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores the superseded narration and does so in conspicuously Japanese-shaped English.

findings.highlight: My position will be in question
findings.evidenceJa: 私の立場がありません
findings.governingReading: Saber says she will have no standing or face as Shirou’s protector if her Master sleeps in such a place.
findings.explanation: Position in question sounds like her office may be challenged and obscures the personal failure of role and dignity she invokes.

findings.governingReading: Taiga alone raises a roaring, theatrical cry of protest.
findings.explanation: Explodes converts performed bluster into a literalized stock reaction and omits the vocal display.

findings.highlight: I can only consider this an insult to the bread.
findings.evidenceJa: パン食を舐めてるとしか思えない
findings.governingReading: Rin says Shirou can only be taking a bread-based breakfast far too lightly.
findings.explanation: Insult to the bread personifies the food and changes criticism of a skimpy meal into a different joke.

findings.governingReading: Shirou rejects Taiga’s supposed majority decision as a rigged contest with a predetermined result.
findings.explanation: Unfair match weakens the accusation that the vote itself is staged and predetermined.
